recipes.name: Mahi Mahi with Coconut Rice and Mango Salsa

steps.text: Whisk olive oil, green onion, lemon juice, red pepper flakes, soy sauce, black pepper, garlic, ginger, and salt together in a bowl. Add mahi mahi; toss to evenly coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and marinate in the refrigerator for 1 hour.

Meanwhile, bring rice, water, chicken bouillon, and 1 tablespoon butter to a boil in a saucepan over high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until liquid has been absorbed, about 20 minutes. Pour in coconut milk and 2 tablespoons sugar; stir. Simmer, uncovered, until coconut milk mostly absorbed.
Set an oven rack in the oven's center and preheat the oven's broiler.

Remove mahi mahi from marinade and shake off excess. Discard remaining marinade. Place fish in a large baking dish in a single layer. Broil in the preheated oven until the fish flakes easily with a fork, 10 to 15 minutes. If fish browns too quickly, cover the baking dish with aluminum foil.
Meanwhile, melt 1 1/2 tablespoons sugar and 1 1/2 teaspoons butter in a skillet over medium-high heat until begins to bubble; stir in mango. Cook and stir until mango is tender, about 5 minutes.
Place 1 mahi mahi fillet over 1 scoop coconut rice; top with mango salsa.

raw_recipe.headline: Mahi Mahi with Coconut Rice and Mango Salsa
raw_recipe.description: This Caribbean-inspired mahi mahi with coconut rice and mango salsa recipe has the perfect balance of sweetness, spice, and tanginess. It's delicious.

review.reviewBody: This dish was amazing! I made a few changes to the original recipe, though. In the marinade, I added a tbsp or so of spiced rum. I used half as much rice since 2 cups of uncooked rice expands into an amount that I can't eat by myself (even 1 cup of dry is still a little too much for 4 servings). I made the biggest changes in the salsa: I cooked the mango following the recipe but then I put it in the refrigerator. I chopped up half a medium red onion, 1 avocado, 1 banana, and a little bit of fresh cilantro. I tossed that with the mango. On the side I wilted some fresh spinach in a little bit of chicken broth seasoned with garlic and red pepper flakes.

* Edited, as I forgot to mention the mango in my first submission.

Delicious. I followed the marinade and rice directions as written, but made a few modest changes to the salsa. I sautéed a 1/4 cup of diced onions and 1/4 cup of diced green bell peppers in 1 tsp of olive oil. I stirred in a 1/2 tsp of Jamaican curry powder to the veggies. I took advantage of some leftovers in the fridge and added a 1/4 cup of diced tomatoes and 1/4 cup of black beans. I added the diced mangos and let them all simmer together for about 10 minutes. Turned out great.

This recipe was so good that even my 2.5 and 5 year old loved it. I did not add red pepper flakes to marinade, and cut back on black pepper because my kids won't eat spicy things. They both asked for more fish, and I still loved the fish without the spice. I cooked rice in rice cooker by mixing all ingredients together before I cooked it. It turned out great. In fact, my daughter and I at the leftover rice with coconut milk and cinnamon for dessert.

This fish was very good but with a couple of tweaks it could be excellent. Unlike many reviewers, I followed the recipe to a "T" and encountered a couple of problems. (1) 2 cups of water is not enough to fully cook the rice even after adding an entire can of coconut milk. I ended up adding another 1/2 cup water after the coconut milk to ensure the rice was cooked. (2) skip the green onion in the marinade. The sliced green onion ended up burning in the broiler. I would just scatter them over the rice when plating. (3) the salsa is very simple as written. Just mango, butter and sugar. It needs the added ingredients others have suggested -- red onion, maybe peppers, some cilantro and maybe some lemon or lime juice. We will definitely be having this dish again, with the above changes, because even my fish-hating daughter loved it!

This is a very good recipe and I made a few changes as others have. I used low-sodium organic chicken stock instead of water (Pacific brand) and low sodium soy sauce. I didn't use butter, since I felt the rice didn't need it. I also used one can of real coconut milk and no sugar, as I will use the leftover rice for curry. I think that using sweetened coconut milk may also be a good substitute and I may try that next time. I only had Swai on hand when I made it and I baked it with the marinade; perfect. I think I will try it with cod next time.

Made this recipe without the mango (though it sounds really good) as it was a last minute dinner and I didn't have mangos. Served it with a cucumber salad dressed with rice vinegar. Added some cilantro (as I had some on hand), chopped, to the rice for color and toasted some coconut flakes to mix into the rice. I got raves - particularly on the rice. It made a beautiful presentation and was SO QUICK AND EASY. Be advised, it makes a lot of rice - I could have easily cut back by half and still had plenty.

This was excellent. I made it with some cod portions I had in the freezer and we loved it. Based on others’ comments, I reduced the crushed red pepper to 1/2 t, halved the rice, reduced sugar and skipped butter in rice (but upped the coconut milk), and made a raw salsa with mango, red pepper, red onion, cilantro, and lime.

This was really good! I did follow some of the reviewers' recommendations by decreasing red pepper flakes to 1 tsp, glad I did. And for the chutney, after cooking mango, I put it in the refrigerator and then added 1/2 chopped red onion, 1 avocado, 1 banana, and cilantro to the mango.

Yummy. Left out the salt in the marinade as it has soy sauce. Works nice to marinate in a flat baking dish and cook with the marinade as there is not so much sauce. Left out the sugar in the rice and put the cut up green onions in with the mango to give it more salsa flavor.

The rice was delicious, fish was tender and delicate, and the marinade was spectacular! (I left out the pepper flakes as my daughter is spicy-avoidant for now.)

To make the mango salsa look a little prettier, I sprinkled in some pre-chopped basil before sautéing. (Oh! I found this great little find in the produce section of about 4 oz of chopped, fresh basil that lasts 4 weeks in the refrigerator! -- a time saver).

This was so good, I can't wait for the leftovers for lunch today!

Will make again for sure. I just did standard jasmine rice, added pineapple and pepper flakes to the salsa, and did a lemon foam to top the fish. The broil was 10 min on lo and then 5 min on hi and it came out so perfectly and crisp on top. Very good.
Was good except sauting already soft mango doesn’t make it salsa. So I found a recipe for mango salsa that included red pepper, lime juice, jalapeño pepper, cilantro, olive oil and garlic.
Followed recipe as is and it tasted amazing. Adding this to our family recipe collection. Thank you!

Good complement of sweet and spicey. Mahi Mahi is a light flakey fish that isn't fishy. Great dish for summer. I added fresh cilantro and lime juice to the rice, and a small amount of red bell pepper to the mango. Be sure to cook down the bell pepper as to not overpower the mango.
For my family of 4 we had no leftovers, wish I had doubled the recipe. Next time I make it I will definitely double it. Very good recipe.
It was pretty good! Especially for the first time making it. I will definitely change it up a bit when I make it again.
I've made this many times over the years. Now that I live in Florida, It is even better!!

The fish and rice are fantastic, but the salsa recipe is missing a whole lot of ingredients. I looked up another to use but Mango butter and sugar is a salsa? I gave three stars because it's the salsa that pushes it over the top.
